stories.headline: Jaden McDaniels scores career-best 34 for Timberwolves in 142-116 rout of Nets
stories.summary: — Jaden McDaniels scored a career-best 34 points and the Minnesota Timberwolves routed the Brooklyn Nets 142-116 on Monday night.
stories.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- — Jaden McDaniels scored a career-best 34 points and the Minnesota Timberwolves routed the Brooklyn Nets 142-116 on Monday night.


Ayo Dosunmu added 23 as six Timberwolves players reached double figures. Terrence Shannon Jr. had 17 points and five assists off the bench, and Jonathan Kuminga scored 15.


McDaniels shot an efficient 12 of 16 from the floor and made all four of his 3-point attempts. He hit a jumper early in the third quarter to reach 30 points for the third time in his regular-season career. The 6-foot-9 forward also had 10 rebounds and six assists.


Minnesota set a season high for points, and Brooklyn allowed its most this season.


The Timberwolves have won two in a row and four of five. The loss was the fifth straight for the struggling Nets.


Julius Randle faced his former team for the first time since the Timberolves traded him to Brooklyn. After two seasons with Minnesota, Randle was dealt in the offseason as part of a four-team swap that helped the Timberwolves land point guard LaMelo Ball from Charlotte.


Ball had 17 points in this one.


Randle led the Nets with 29 points in his return to Minnesota. He was honored by the Wolves with a pregame video tribute.


Mikel Brown Jr. added 17 points for Brooklyn, all in the first half.


Brooklyn shot a season-best 50% from 3-point range (18 of 36), but a hot shooting night wasn't enough for a Nets team near the bottom of the Eastern Conference standings.


Up next
Nets: Play at Milwaukee on Wednesday.


Timberwolves: Play at Oklahoma City on Wednesday.


------

stories.headline: Price tag for Tassie's new AFL stadium goes up, again
stories.summary: The estimated cost of a new 23,000-seat waterfront venue, set to eventually become the home of the Tasmania Devils, has risen again.
stories.body:
The estimated cost for Tasmania's new AFL stadium has gone up again, this time by $100 million.

Updated figures for the 23,000-seat roofed waterfront venue at Macquarie Point in Hobart were released on Tuesday.

It puts the price tag on the stadium at $1.23 billion, above the previous $1.13 billion mark set about 12 months ago.

The new estimate reflects an increase in the cost of construction, sustained high oil and materials prices, higher labour costs and its complexity, the state government said.

There is also $132 million to be spent on broader precinct infrastructure, as well as project delivery costs of $183 million, which both sit outside the $1.23 billion.

There is also a "contingency" dollar amount which has not been specified.

Premier Jeremy Rockliff previously pledged to cap Tasmania's contribution to the build at $875 million but said that would likely rise via more borrowings to cover the $100 million rise.

"Major projects are always challenging, but as a state we must be able to say yes to opportunity, new industry and economic growth," he said.

The government has asked the AFL and federal government to contribute more to the project, Mr Rockliff said.

The stadium is expected to be ready for the 2031 AFL season and was a condition of the Tasmania Devils being granted a licence to enter into the national competition in 2028.

Its construction was initially budgeted at $715 million.

The release of updated costs came ahead of schedule, with the state government bowing to political pressure to make figures public before the end of the parliamentary year.

In mid-October, BESIX Watpac was announced as the preferred builder - a final contract is set to be signed by the end of 2026.

The final contract price was unlikely to differ from the $1.23 billion estimate, Mr Rockliff said.

The stadium has proven deeply divisive in Tasmania, amid rising budget debt and a stretched health system and under-pressure services.

The AFL is contributing $15 million, with the federal government chipping in $240 million for the stadium and broader precinct.

stories.headline: David Moyes accepts James Tarkowski red card in Everton defeat to Brentford
stories.summary: Everton manager David Moyes said he understood why James Tarkowski was shown a straight red card in the 4-0 defeat to Brentford.
stories.body:
LONDON -- Everton manager David Moyes said he understood why James Tarkowski was shown a straight red card in the 4-0 defeat to Brentford despite initially thinking it was the incorrect decision.

The Everton captain was penalised for a tackle on Yegor Yarmolyuk in the 40th minute, where he got the ball but caught the Brentford midfielder high up on the shin with his follow through.

Referee Craig Pawson had initially shown Tarkowski a yellow card, but he was forced to reconsider his decision by VAR and subsequently upgraded it to a red card.

Everton were already 2-0 down by this point courtesy of a Keane Lewis-Potter brace and the red card dented any chances they had of producing a comeback. Second-half goals from Vitaly Janelt and Fábio Carvalho added to Everton's misery and saw them fall to ninth in the Premier League.

"My first feeling at the time was I didn't think it was red because I thought James easily got to the ball before. He easily got to the ball before the Brentford player, so I would have said that the Brentford player was a bit late in getting there," Moyes said in his post-match news conference.

"But obviously after I've seen it again, I've seen Tarki's boots are a bit higher so I can understand why the position went against us."

Unsurprisingly, Brentford boss Keith Andrews was also in agreement with the decision to send off Tarkowski.

"I don't think he can tackle like that in this day and age. We've also been on the wrong side of some decisions in recent weeks that have cost us. So I'm certainly not going to challenge that one," Andrews said.

The 4-0 win over Everton pushes Brentford into sixth place and puts them in firm contention for a Champions League spot. In the previous two years, the top five teams have qualified for Europe's elite competition.

Brentford have never qualified for any tier of European football, missing out on the Conference League last year due to goal difference.

- Vitaly Janelt hits stunner as Brentford stroll to victory over 10-man Everton

- Man United to appeal Leny Yoro red card against Liverpool - sources

- Kevin De Bruyne: Man City achievements will not be tainted if appeal fails

When asked if European qualification was the primary target this season, Andrews said: "We're just doing what we do. I think we set out this season looking to be better than last season. I think if that happens, naturally we might be flying to different destinations next year.

"So we've got a very competitive squad. We've got an amazing group of young men that want to strive and want to get better. I think if we continue with that mindset, we'll hopefully be in a good place."

Everton host Liverpool in the Merseyside derby on Sunday, while Brentford travel to Manchester United the day before.

stories.headline: MLB offers higher minimum salaries while union eyes local media revenue sharing
stories.summary: MLB suggested more measures Monday to get players paid earlier in their careers while the players union agreed to share local media equally among the 30 teams.
stories.body:
In a series of proposals aimed toward making up ground with a lockout looming, Major League Baseball suggested more measures Monday to get players paid earlier in their careers while the MLB Players Association agreed to share local media equally among the 30 teams.

League owners attempted to sweeten their cap-and-floor proposal by increasing the minimum salary to $1 million in 2027 -- a $220,000 bump from 2026 -- and providing centrally funded bonuses to arbitration-eligible players who settle without a hearing and veterans signing one-year contracts.

Those measures, though, are unlikely to create much momentum with a players' union that is categorically opposed to a salary cap and has vehemently turned one down at every juncture.

MLB spokesperson Glen Caplin refuted the rationale as part of his statement on Monday, saying: "The Union's claim that our proposal would negatively impact 'all categories of players' is not accurate. To the contrary, especially in light of today's new proposals to increase the minimum salary, provide an automatic signing bonus for arbitration-eligible players and offer a new veteran signing bonus, MLB's proposals on the table would provide benefits to most players in every stage of their career."

MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer said the league's proposals "don't add a single dollar in overall player compensation," alluding to the fact that all of their concessions are being made within the same cap-and-floor system.

MLB made its initial offer on May 28, suggesting a $245.3 million cap and a $171.2 million floor beginning in 2027. On Nov. 3, MLB proposed pushing it back to 2028, with a projected cap of $258.2 million and a floor of $180.2 million.

The union has repeatedly referred to the cap-and-floor system as a "zero-sum game" in which players compete against one another for finite amounts of money, as opposed to the current free market.

"Any supposed benefits to certain classes of players are simply taken out of the pockets of other players and are vastly outweighed by the negative effects of the cap and MLB's other restrictions," Meyer said in a statement. "These negative effects include, but are not limited to, a drastic reduction in overall player compensation and benefits, the end of fully guaranteed contracts, and dramatic restrictions on players' career choices and freedom to contract."

The current collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1, at which point owners are expected to impose a lockout that would freeze transactions and cut off all communication between teams and major league players.

The previous lockout occurred after the expiration of the last CBA in December of 2021 and lasted 99 days. MLB's insistence on a salary cap, which prompted the cancellation of the 1994 World Series, have people throughout the sport fearing that this lockout could last much longer.

MLB proposed equal distribution of local media as part of its initial cap proposal, adding that the concept would eliminate the territorial exclusivity of regional sports networks and thus do away with blackouts. The MLBPA formally agreed to that form of revenue sharing on Monday, albeit outside of a cap-and-floor system, while maintaining prior proposals aimed toward rewarding low-revenue teams that win.

Under its proposal, the MLBPA says low-revenue teams would receive an increase of more than $1 billion in assistance over the life of a new CBA.

On Monday, the MLBPA proposed an increase from roughly $700 million to more than $950 million for low-revenue markets from 2026 to 2027, while maintaining $20 million monetary rewards for revenue-sharing recipients that either qualify for the postseason or fail to qualify but finish with a better record than the worst playoff team. Revenue-sharing recipients who finish with a record above .500 would receive a $10 million reward under the MLBPA's revenue-sharing model, which originally allowed teams to keep more stadium-related revenue.

In addition to a $1 million minimum salary in 2027, MLB proposed a $100,000 bonus for players who receive a full year of service time and spend less than half the season on the injured list. The league also established a centrally funded signing bonus equal to 5% of an arbitration-eligible player's base salary if he agrees to terms without the need for a hearing. MLB said 93% of players settled their arbitration cases without a hearing under the current CBA.

Under the league's proposal, each team can reward a $500,000 bonus to a veteran player -- one with at least six years of service time -- who signs a one-year contract valued at $10 million or less. MLB once again agreed to increase the pre-arbitration bonus pool by 30%, from $50 million in 2026 to $65 million in 2027, and to reduce free agency to five years for 30-and-older players.

Those players can still be kept by their teams if offered a one-year contract equal to the average salary of the 125 highest-paid players, the same model used to determine qualifying offers under the current system. MLB agreed to eliminate the qualifying offer for six-year free agents.

To the union, though, it's all essentially window dressing at this point.

The overall pot of money for major league players would be fixed under MLB's proposal; the distribution of money is simply different. The league fully acknowledges that is the case. Its hope is to eventually sway a large enough percentage of the player population to attain the cap it so desperately desires. As part of a fact sheet distributed to media members Monday, the league included a chart noting when every player would qualify for free agency under its current proposal.

"Every other major U.S. sport has a salary cap and floor system to limit payroll disparity, and the fact remains that growth in player compensation has been slower in baseball than every one of those leagues," Caplin said in his statement. "MLB is trying to reach an agreement with the players by meeting their objectives on a number of important issues, including earlier access to free agency and increased compensation for players earlier in their careers."

stories.headline: Qatar Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Formula 1 heads to Qatar for the second leg of its final triple header of the 2026 season.
stories.body:
Formula 1 heads to Qatar for the second leg of its final triple header of the 2026 season.

Max Verstappen fended off his rivals to take a stunning victory under the lights at the Las Vegas Grand Prix last time out.

McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri took the final spots on the podium.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 22nd round.

- Max Verstappen mocks George Russell in brutal outburst: 'So far below my level'

- Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc 'unmanageable' - Ferrari boss

- Max Verstappen, George Russell's latest war of words unlikely to stay in Vegas

Qatar Grand Prix schedule
All times in GMT

Friday, November 27

Practice One: 1.30 p.m. - 2.30 p.m.

Practice Two: 5 p.m. - 6 p.m.

Saturday, November 28

Final Practice: 2.30 p.m. - 3.30 p.m.

Qualifying: 6 p.m. - 7 p.m.

Sunday, November 29

Qatar Grand Prix: 4 p.m.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Qatar Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Lusail Circuit

The Qatar Grand Prix takes place under the floodlights at the Lusail Circuit. It is one of the most demanding on the calendar with long straights and sweeping high-speed corners coupled with intense heat and humidity, making conditions for the cars and drivers difficult.

It was originally built as a motorbike circuit before it joined the F1 calendar in 2021 on a 10-year contract. Qatar did not host a race in 2022 as they focused on the FIFA World Cup.

Qatar Grand Prix

Circuit: Lusail International Circuit; Lusail, Qatar

Previous winners in Qatar

2021: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2023: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2024: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2025: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 2021

Laps: 57 laps of 5.4km

Lap record: 1:22.384, Lando Norris (2024)

Most wins: Verstappen (2023, 2024 and 2025). Lewis Hamilton (2021) is the only other winner.

Most poles: Hamilton (2021), Verstappen (2023), George Russell (2024) and Piastri (2025) have each taken pole.

Weather forecast

The weather for the Qatar Grand Prix is forecast to be sunny with a gentle breeze across the weekend. It's a night race so conditions are dry with highs of 24°C on Sunday.

What happened last time out?

McLaren's Piastri pipped teammate Norris to pole position as the battle for the world title continued with two races remaining.

During the race, Red Bull's Verstappen benefited from a McLaren strategy error to win his seventh race of the season, taking the three-way title race to the season finale in Abu Dhabi.

Piastri was leading the race and Norris was running in third, but the Papaya team decided against pitting under the Safety Car. Piastri ended the race in second, with Norris in fourth.

Who will win this year?

Verstappen looked unstoppable in Las Vegas and will be targeting his fifth win of the season in Qatar.

Mercedes' Russell was well in the mix last time out but will be looking to respond after Verstappen said the Englishman was "so far below his level" as their feud intensified.

Both teams look strong, so the rivalry could well continue in Qatar. Drivers up and down the grid will also be limited to 27 laps on each set of tyres, which will play massively into teams' strategies.

Tensions between Ferrari teammates Hamilton and Charles Leclerc continue to heat up after boss Fred Vasseur labelled them "unmanageable."

Don't count out new world champion Kimi Antonelli who is always one to watch after an impressive season.

stories.headline: Tom Brady tops list of athletes who became owners
stories.summary: The legendary quarterback is a member of an exclusive list of athletes that includes LeBron James, Serena Williams and Wayne Gretzky.
stories.body:
Tom Brady is getting (back) into the ownership game.

On Friday, sources confirmed to ESPN and NFL Network that the former superstar quarterback had bought shares in the English soccer giants Chelsea. Brady's purchasing of Chelsea shares comes after he departed the ownership group of another English club, EFL Championship side Birmingham City, earlier in the month after originally becoming a minority owner with a 3.3% stake.

Brady's latest interest isn't his only foray into the world of ownership -- he also owns a 5% minority stake in the Las Vegas Raiders, purchased in 2024, and he also has a stake in the Las Vegas Aces.

The NFL legend is far from the first athlete, active or former, to enter the ownership sphere. Here are other athletes who are now team owners:

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Atlético Madrid

In October 26 news broke that the star Oklahoma City Thunder guard would be joining the club as an investor.

"I am excited to officially join the group of shareholders of Atlético de Madrid," Gilgeous-Alexander said in the club's post. "This is a club with a long history at the top of European football, and I am grateful for the opportunity to be part of its future."

Jason Kidd -- Everton

In April 2025, English Premier League club Everton announced that then-Dallas Mavericks coach Jason Kidd would be adding a different title to his résumé: ownership group member. The news came after Kidd joined Roundhouse Capital Holdings, which is part of the Friedkin Group -- the U.S. firm that completed its takeover of Everton's ownership the previous December.

Vince Carter, Tracy McGrady, Jozy Altidore -- Buffalo Bills

In December 2024, the Bills announced Carter, McGrady and Altidore were among 10 limited partners the team was adding to its ownership group. Both McGrady (New York Knicks) and Altidore (New York Red Bulls) played for New York-area teams, while Carter spent time with the Brooklyn Nets (who were known as the New Jersey Nets at the time) and was McGrady's teammate on the Toronto Raptors (who are closer to Buffalo than NYC-based teams).

Tom Brady -- Las Vegas Aces, Las Vegas Raiders, Chelsea

The Las Vegas Aces, the reigning WNBA champions, have added to their championship credentials. Seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady acquired a minority stake in the team whose majority owner is Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis.

"I have always been a huge fan of women's sports, and I admire the work that the Aces' players, staff, and the WNBA continue to do to grow the sport and empower future generations of athletes," Brady said in a statement. "To be able to contribute in any way to that mission as a member of the Aces organization is an incredible honor."

Brady attended an Aces game in May 2022 and sent gifts to star Kelsey Plum. Plum and other Aces players were excited to have Brady as part of the team.

He also added the Las Vegas Raiders to his resume after his purchase of minority stake in the franchise was approved by NFL teams owners on Tuesday. The deal was agreed on in May 2023, but it took owners 17 months to give their approval over concerns he was receiving too much of a discount from majority owner Mark Davis.

Brady was also a minority owner of Birmingham City, a club in English soccer's second-tier Championship, but sold his shares in November 2026. He purchased shares in Chelsea later that month.

Lewis Hamilton -- Denver Broncos

The Broncos' ownership group added racing royalty in August 2022. Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton has a stake with the Walton-Penner group, which purchased the team in June 2022.

Hamilton, 37, has the Formula One record for most race wins and has won the Formula One title seven times. The ownership group, which purchased the team for $4.65 billion, is led by Walmart heir Rob Walton and includes former U.S. Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice, who also has a stake.

In April, Hamilton joined with Serena Williams in a consortium led by former Liverpool chairman Martin Broughton in an attempt to buy Premier League club Chelsea.

"He is a champion competitor who knows what it takes to lead a winning team," Walton said in a statement.

Marshawn Lynch -- Seattle Kraken

Lynch spent 13 seasons in Seattle with the Seahawks, but his new sports venture in the state of Washington is on the ice. On April 18, he joined the Seattle Kraken ownership team as a minority investor. The former NFL running back will be a part of the NHL's "Hockey is for Everyone" campaign and Kraken owner Tod Leiweke said Lynch expressed interest in shadowing him to learn hockey CEO operations.

"This is something I never would have imagined," Lynch said to CNBC in a statement. "I always dreamed of playing on a professional team but owning one is something special. As I look back on some of my accomplishments...I'm [going to] continue to count my blessings."

Grammy Award-winning artist and Seattle native Macklemore also joined the Kraken ownership team with Lynch.

Wayne Gretzky, Steve Nash and Dustin Johnson -- Las Vegas Desert Dogs

Wayne Gretzky is a big lacrosse guy? Yep, you read that right. The Great One may have made his name on the ice, but before Gretzky was the pride of the Edmonton Oilers he was a bona fide lax bro.

"The national sport of Canada is box lacrosse," Gretzky said. "I started playing lacrosse on a team at the age of six and played all the way until I was 16 years old. I have a great love for the game in the sense I really think that box lacrosse was such a crucial part of the success I ultimately had in ice hockey."

Because of this, it shouldn't be completely surprising that the hockey legend is linking up with 2020 Masters champion Dustin Johnson, NBA Hall of Famer and current Brooklyn Nets head coach Steve Nash and Nets owner Joe Tsai as part of a star-studded ownership group for the National Lacrosse League's newest expansion team in Las Vegas, the Desert Dogs.

Dwyane Wade -- Utah Jazz

Seeing Dwyane Wade support any team other than the Miami Heat is decidedly jarring. In April, the three-time NBA champion purchased an ownership stake in the Utah Jazz, joining majority owner and team governor Ryan Smith, and expressed a desire to take an active role in the franchise. D. Wade made good on his promise. He could be seen courtside throughout the season; he took action when an unsettling fan incident went down during the postseason, and he became a mentor to then-Jazz star Donovan Mitchell.

The former Miami Heat star also added to his portfolio with something a bit closer to home. Wade, a Chicago native, joined the ownership group of the WNBA's Chicago Sky.

"It's a great opportunity to be a part of the league in its very early stages. ... Growth is going to happen, and so I want to be a part of the growth of this league," Wade said.

Kevin Durant -- Philadelphia Union, NJ/NY Gotham FC

In June 2020, Brooklyn Nets star Kevin Durant purchased a 5% stake in MLS' Philadelphia Union, and he has an option to purchase an additional 5% at a later date. Durant also had engaged in talks about purchasing part of D.C. United the year prior, but he said the discussion never progressed.

Durant expanded his portfolio in May of this year, after being named as a minority owner of the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) club NJ/NY Gotham FC.

Thirty Five Ventures (35V), a company co-founded by the two-time NBA champion and entrepreneur Rich Kleiman, made a significant investment to acquire a stake in the club, marking the company's second investment in a professional soccer team.

Renee Montgomery -- Atlanta Dream

Former Atlanta Dream guard Renee Montgomery made history in February as part of a three-member investor group that was approved to purchase the team. Montgomery is the first former player to become both an owner and executive of a WNBA franchise. The ownership change followed pressure on former Republican Sen. Kelly Loeffler to sell her share of the Dream, after she angered WNBA players with her opposition to the league's racial justice initiatives.

Patrick Mahomes -- Kansas City Royals

Patrick Mahomes is no stranger to winning. While the Kansas City Royals can't exactly say the same, you can't rule out that the quarterback's winning ways might rub off on the franchise now that he is part of their ownership group. If Mahomes' status as an icon in Kansas City was in question (it wasn't), this move surely cemented it. Becoming a baseball owner made sense on several levels for the Chiefs' QB1. Not only was Mahomes -- who played baseball in college -- a legitimate pro prospect, his father, Pat Mahomes, spent 11 seasons in Major League Baseball. He also had to find some way to put that $503 million contract extension to good use.

Venus and Serena Williams -- Miami Dolphins, Angel City FC

Winning major titles and making history, that's what the Williams sisters do. In 2009, Venus and Serena became the first Black female minority owners in the NFL by purchasing a part of the Miami Dolphins. Musicians Jimmy Buffett, Gloria and Emilio Estefan, Fergie and Marc Anthony also bought shares in the team -- the Dolphins' ownership group is nothing if not eclectic. Then, last year, Serena Williams became part of the star-studded Angel City FC ownership group bringing a NWSL team to Los Angeles in 2022.

Mia Hamm, Abby Wambach and Julie Foudy -- Angel City FC

When Angel City FC arrived on the scene it did so in style. Before we even knew the Los Angeles based NWSL club's name, we knew it had superstar backing like no other. Among the 14 former USWNT players who are part of the group are Mia Hamm, Abby Wambach and Julie Foudy. I would have named Lauren Holiday, Shannon Boxx, Rachel Buehler, Amanda Cromwell, Joy Fawcett, Tisha Venturini Hoch, Angela Hucles, Shannon MacMillan, Saskia Webber and sisters Lorrie Fair Allen and Ronnie Fair Sullins, but I was really trying to stay true to my whole "I'm only going to name 20 athletes" thing from the intro. There are also a bunch of celebrities in the mix, but we don't have that kind of time.

Michael Jordan -- Charlotte Hornets

While we're on the subject of owners who haven't had the type of success we grew accustomed to in their playing days, I would be remiss if I didn't mention the GOAT. In 2010, Michael Jordan became the first ex-player to be a majority owner in the league when the NBA's Board of Governors unanimously approved his $275 million bid to buy the then Charlotte Bobcats in his home state of North Carolina. After a decade of underwhelming years, things look to be on the up for the now Hornets with Rookie of the Year LaMelo Ball providing a long-awaited spark in the organization. Never forget when his dad said he could beat MJ one-on-one ... good times.

Alex Rodriguez -- Minnesota Timberwolves, Minnesota Lynx

I don't know what part of this purchase feels less ideal to me, that Alex Rodriguez and his 50-50 business partner Marc Lore are only pursuing acquiring the Minnesota Timberwolves and Lynx after their original plan to buy the New York Mets failed or that Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards had no idea who former MLB star A-Rod was. Either way, the $1.5 billion deal is expected to close around July 1.

David Beckham -- Inter Miami

David Beckham, iconic soccer player and remains-to-be-seen owner. Beckham -- who is incredibly hands on with the franchise -- is part of an ownership group which was initially called Miami Beckham United but now operates under the name Miami Freedom Park LLC. Beckham and Inter Miami have seemingly been riddled with controversy since the club's inception in 2018. But all those problems could be a thing of the past if Lionel Messi decides to head to MLS. Hey, stranger things have happened.

LeBron James -- Liverpool

Back in 2011, LeBron James and manager Maverick Carter became minority owners of Premier League club Liverpool after Fenway Sports Group, which purchased the team in 2010, became the sole marketer of James' global rights. The deal has turned out to be pretty lucrative for James -- his original stake in the club, valued at about $6.5 million, had grown to about $32 million as of 2018. In 2019, Liverpool won the Premier League for their first top-flight league title in thirty years.

James Harden -- Houston Dynamo, Houston Dash

James Harden might not be in Houston anymore, but the former Rockets superstar's presence is still felt in the city. The Beard purchased a 5% stake in the group that controls MLS' Houston Dynamo and NWSL's Houston Dash in 2019. Boxer Oscar De La Hoya is also part of the group. The Dash won their first NWSL title last year, so he's probably feeling pretty good about that investment.

Russell Wilson and Ken Griffey Jr. -- Seattle Sounders

What do Russell Wilson, Ken Griffey Jr. and Macklemore have in common? They are all part of the Seattle Sounders' ownership group. Wilson, along with his wife, musician Ciara, purchased a stake in the team in 2019 -- just in time for them to win an MLS Cup title. Griffey Jr. and his family followed suit in November 2020.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic -- Hammaraby

Seemingly everything Zlatan does makes people react intensely, and that remained true when he purchased part of Swedish team Hammaraby back in 2019. Fans of Malmo, another Swedish team where Zlatan started his professional career, reacted by vandalizing a statue of Zlatan outside the team's home stadium, placing a toilet seat around one of its arms.

Magic Johnson -- Los Angeles Dodgers

Big LA guy. In 2012, Lakers great Magic Johnson was part of a group that bought the Los Angeles Dodgers from Frank McCourt for a record $2 billion. At the time, the price shattered the mark for a sports franchise. Magic kept it real at the time of purchase when explaining his role in recruiting free agents, saying that while he can't talk hitting or pitching with players, he "can talk winning." If recent history is any indication (in case you blacked out all of 2020 -- the Dodgers won the World Series), it worked.

stories.headline: 'Little disappointing': Munster makes call on Storm offer
stories.summary: Melbourne's fight to keep Cameron Munster and Harry Grant has been made harder after the former rejected the club's latest offer.
stories.body:
Cameron Munster has declared all options are on the table after officially rejecting a deal to stay in Melbourne and labelling the Storm's latest offer as "disappointing".

With Melbourne already facing a battle to retain Harry Grant, the Storm is now officially fighting a retention war on two fronts after Munster's decision.

The Melbourne superstar admitted on Tuesday that Grant's future could play a role in his own call, as well as Craig Bellamy's impending retirement at the end of 2027.

As it stands Munster will not take up an offer from the Storm that is understood to have been for one year with an option for a second.

"I have declined it," the Queensland State of Origin captain said at a Maroons sponsor announcement with Westpac.

"I am not saying I am going to leave Melbourne. Just with the terms and conditions that they put out to me, it is probably something that is a little disappointing.

"But it's a business, I am not stupid."

Munster admitted his own form had not been good enough for the Storm last season as they missed the finals for the first time in his career.

And in turn, the 32-year-old conceded the offer may have been as a result of that.

"That (offer) just makes my job a little bit harder. But it's also a bit of a challenge saying I am not where I need to be," he said.

"Maybe I need to be a little bit better to earn that contract that we're looking from.

"And maybe it is a little bit of a kick up the bum from them. I am not too sure where we'll go from here but all options are open at the moment."

Munster's rejection comes after Grant met with Gold Coast officials last Friday and officially received an offer to join the Titans.

It is understood Melbourne's offer for the Queensland dummy-half will either be worth similar or more than the Titans.

But Gold Coast are hopeful of luring the hooker north, given his relationship with ex-Maroons assistant coach Josh Hannay and prop Tino Fa'asuamaleaui.

NSW prop Stefano Utoikamanu is also off contract at the end of next year and has also been linked to the Sydney Roosters.

At the same time Bellamy's retirement at the end of next season is proving a challenge for the Storm, given he is like a father figure to Munster.

"When you look at someone like Craig as a coach, he is a great coach and I have so much respect and have admired him for such a long time," Munster said.

"It's going to be different at the club. I'm not too sure where the club wants to go with all that stuff.

"I don't know who they are going to get and I'm sure it will be a daunting job coming after him."

Munster also confirmed he will likely follow the Cameron Smith route and give away representative football at some point to focus on club duties.

"It definitely has (crossed my mind)," Munster said.

"The hard thing for me is giving up the captaincy.

"Once I start declining (I will look at it) and I thought I was declining. But after my last few games for the World Cup I am pretty confident I can get back to that."

stories.headline: Vilardi's 2nd career hat trick helps the Jets to a 4-2 win over the Mammoth
stories.summary: — Gabriel Vilardi had a hat trick and the Winnipeg Jets hung on for a 4-2 victory over the Utah Mammoth on Monday night.
stories.body:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba -- — Gabriel Vilardi had a hat trick and the Winnipeg Jets hung on for a 4-2 victory over the Utah Mammoth on Monday night.


Morgan Barron also had a goal for the Jets (12-9-4). Kyle Connor picked up two assists. Stuart Skinner made 34 saves for Winnipeg, which is 8-1-1 in its past 10 games and finished a four-game homestand 2-1-1.


Andrew Peeke and Lawson Crouse scored for the Mammoth (12-10-3). Sebastian Cossa stopped 11 shots.


It was a back-and-forth, high-scoring game in the opening period.


Vilardi got things going at 5:11, Peeke replied 67 seconds later, Vilardi notched his second assist 68 seconds after that and Crouse made it 2-2 at 10:22. Barron broke the tie at 14:00.


Vilardi scored an empty-netter with 7 seconds remaining in the third. It was his second career hat trick. The other was April 4, 2024, against the Calgary Flames.


It was Winnipeg’s first victory over Utah since Jan. 24, 2025, a span of six games (2-3-1).


Heading into the game, Utah led the NHL with 21 goals from defensemen, now 22 with Peeke’s goal.


Utah forward Dylan Guenther, who had missed the past six games with injury, and Clayton Keller (illness), returned to the top line. Logan Cooley extended his point streak to four games (one goal, four assists).


Up next
Mammoth: At the Minnesota Wild on Wednesday.


Jets: At the Boston Bruins on Wednesday.


------

stories.headline: Siakam scores 20 and comes up big late as Pacers snap 4-game skid with 125-120 win over Thunder
stories.summary: — Pascal Siakam scored 20 points, including a 3-pointer with 44.4 seconds to go, and Kelly Oubre Jr. added a season-high 20 points to help the Indiana Pacers snap a four-game losing streak with a 125-120 victory over the Oklahoma City Thunder on...
stories.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- — Pascal Siakam scored 20 points, including a 3-pointer with 44.4 seconds to go, and Kelly Oubre Jr. added a season-high 20 points to help the Indiana Pacers snap a four-game losing streak with a 125-120 victory over the Oklahoma City Thunder on Monday night.


The Pacers finished 15 of 37 on 3-pointers and looked much more like the team that made the 2025 NBA Finals by pushing the tempo, knocking down long-range shots and spreading the scoring. Six players scored in double figures, including Jalen Slawson with 16, Andrew Nembhard with 15 and Ivica Zubac who had 14 points and 15 rebounds. Obi Toppin finished with 17 points and six rebounds.


Two-time league MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander kept short-handed Oklahoma City close with 38 points. Kenrich Williams made four 3s and finished with 20 points, and Isaiah Hartenstein finished with 18 points and nine rebounds. But it wasn't quite enough to prevent the Thunder from suffering a second straight loss.


What was supposed to be the first matchup between Tyrese Haliburton and the Thunder since Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals never materialized.


Haliburton missed his 14th straight game with a strained left hamstring and only four of Monday's starters also started that Game 7 — Gilgeous-Alexander and Hartenstein of the Thunder and Nembhard and Siakam for the Pacers.


Indiana never trailed after going on a 9-0 run to take a 27-19 lead late in the first quarter. The Pacers still led 56-51 and extended the margin to 70-58 in the third quarter before a back-and-forth final quarter.


The Thunder cut the deficit to one twice in the final 1:31, but Siakam answered each time with a jumper, the second a 3 to give Indiana a 123-119 with 44.4 seconds left, and Oubre's late block of a layup preserved the lead.


Up next
Thunder: Return home to face Minnesota on Wednesday.


Pacers: Get a three-day break before hosting Philadelphia on Friday.


------

stories.headline: Houston says Herrera available for Dynamo playoff opener amid MLS probe
stories.summary: MLS is gathering information regarding the reported arrest of Houston Dynamo FC midfielder Héctor Herrera for suspicion of driving while intoxicated ahead of the team's first game of the playoffs.
stories.body:
MLS is gathering information regarding the reported arrest of Houston Dynamo FC midfielder Héctor Herrera for suspicion of driving while intoxicated ahead of the team's first game of the best-of-three round one series against the San Jose Earthquakes on Nov. 24.

"Major League Soccer is aware of an incident involving Houston Dynamo midfielder Héctor Herrera," MLS said in a statement to ESPN. "The League is gathering additional information and will refrain from further comment pending a review of the matter."

Houston Dynamo head coach Ben Olsen confirmed that as of Monday, Nov. 23, Herrera is eligible to feature in the playoff match against the Earthquakes.

Multiple reports said Herrera was charged with suspicion of DWI in Montgomery County, Texas, on Saturday. The Dynamo told ESPN on Sunday the club was aware of an incident involving Herrera.

"It's all in the league's hands. So far, he's available to play tomorrow," Olsen said in a press conference Monday.

Olsen added that Herrera's situation is not ideal, but does not present a distraction for the rest of the team ahead of the playoff match.

"The incident in question is Friday night, all right? And don't want to get into too many details. Is it ideal? No, but by and large, it's not a huge distraction. It's not ideal. But, you know, the group is a very healthy one, and we all have love for Hector, and when these things creep up, you deal with them in the right way, through process," Olsen added.

"It's been addressed, and it's been put to bed.  The team is in a good place. This is not any excuse. Throughout the season, things like this happened, you know? And you, whether it's family members or, you know, things happen throughout seasons, and you address them, and you move on.

"And this isn't, again, the first thing that's happened this year, that we've had to address as a group, and all our focus right now is on trying to advance against a really good team, and I really don't even want to get into any more questions on Hector, frankly, because I think right now, the focus should be on our group, and the opportunity in front of us against San Jose."

Herrera previously faced MLS sanctions when he was sent off in 2024 for spitting on a referee. The Houston Dynamo chose to deny his 2025 contract extension following the incident, prior to re-signing Herrera in 2026.

The midfielder briefly featured for Liga MX side Toluca in 2025, before returning to MLS.

Herrera has recorded nine goals and 25 assists in 99 MLS regular season and playoff appearances for the Dynamo across four seasons. He played in 30 regular season games in 2026 since rejoining the club.

ESPN writer Cesar Hernandez contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Heeney headlines returning Swans at pre-season training
stories.summary: After months of off-field turmoil in the fallout from the Pullman Hotel scandal, the Sydney Swans have welcomed back four AFL players for pre-season training.
stories.body:
The Sydney Swans have welcomed back their embattled AFL quartet to training after months of off-field turmoil following the Pullman Hotel scandal.

Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, James Jordon and Riley Bice signalled their intent to resurrect their playing careers by taking part in the club's first-to-fourth-year pre-season training on Monday.

High-profile forward Tom Papley was also in attendance at Sydney's Bat and Ball Oval after being slapped with a three-game ban by the AFL for a positive roadside drug test.

Monday's session marked the first time Heeney, Warner, Bice and Jordon have officially trained with the Swans since serving a season-ending suspension for what the club termed a "serious breach of expected club behaviour and standards".

That AFL-endorsed suspension was also served by now-North Melbourne player Nick Blakey.

Separate from the bans, Heeney, Warner, Jordon and Blakey were under investigation after three women made reports of sexual assault to Victoria Police.

Police have since confirmed the players would not be charged due to insufficient evidence.

Civil claims are still being prepared against relevant parties.

Monday's session was a relaxed affair, with the club also welcoming draftees Caylen Murray, Mason McGroder, Mitchell Knevitt and Brady Wright.

Players undertook the usual pre-season conditioning programs, doing running drills before moving on to contest work and a short match simulation.

It wasn't the first time Heeney, Warner, Jordon and Rice had trained with teammates, having done informal sessions at Centennial Park.

Papley, one of the team's most experienced players, returned to training as he prepares to face Waverley Local Court for driving with a suspended licence on November 26.

The 30-year-old was pulled over by NSW Police for a random roadside drug test on November 2, with checks revealing his licence was suspended due to non-payment of a parking fine.

The initial roadside test returned a positive reading, and a secondary sample of oral fluid was taken.

That secondary sample returned a positive roadside test for the presence of cocaine and MDMA.

On top of his AFL ban for conduct unbecoming, Papley was fined $722 by police and his licence will be suspended for three months.

Papley spent most of Monday's training session with the rehabilitation group alongside fellow forwards Logan McDonald and Hayden McLean after undergoing surgery on both knees.

He suffered a grade-two medial collateral ligament strain in his right knee in the club's preliminary final loss to Fremantle, before undergoing an arthroscopy on his left knee to address a historic issue.

Papley will miss all pre-season matches and the club's opening rounds against Geelong, Essendon and GWS.

stories.headline: NFL Week 11 arrivals: Tee Higgins pays homage to Fiona the Hippo ahead of 'MNF'
stories.summary: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
stories.body:
The forecast affected the game plan for how NFL players put together their Week 11 looks.

And Sunday's arrivals called for a little more wardrobe strategy.

With morning temperatures near freezing in Denver before an afternoon climb into the 40s, players arriving for the Raiders-Broncos game had an opening for coats and chunky knits. Showers in Chicago could have made weatherproof outerwear a smart finishing touch, while temperatures approaching 70 in Southern California gave the New York Jets and Los Angeles Chargers room to keep things lighter.

On the East Coast, Sunday's forecast left room for fall outfits without going full winter. Morning temperatures in the 50s in Buffalo gave Miami Dolphins and Buffalo Bills players an opening for sweaters and light jackets, while Jacksonville Jaguars and New York Giants arrivals in East Rutherford, New Jersey, called for similar layers under cloudy skies, with rain possible later in the day.

From practical layers to outfits built for the spotlight, here are the standout arrivals from Week 11.

Monday night drip
Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins sported a tribute to a local legend for his pregame fit ahead of Monday Night Football against the Washington Commanders.

Higgins wore a "Fiona the Hippo" long sleeve for his arrival at Northwest Stadium. Fiona was one of the most beloved animals at the Cincinnati Zoo but died on Thursday after ingesting a hat thrown by a child that ended up in the hippo enclosure.

The Cincinnati star receiver, who owns a jellyfish tank at his home, is among many in the Cincinnati sports community and around the country who have offered their condolences following Fiona's death. -- Ben Baby

Sunday's best
Playing in Mexico City on "Sunday Night Football," players from the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings arrived in looks fit for the location. 49ers tight end George Kittle rocked a mask and shirt that paid homage to luchador Penta, while Fred Warner had a Mexico national team kit on. Vikings running back Aaron Jones Sr. kept his sombrero trend alive in a full mariachi look.

Denver Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton paid homage to former Broncos linebacker Tom Jackson by wearing Jackson's jersey before facing the Las Vegas Raiders. Jackson, a fixture at ESPN as a Hall of Fame broadcaster, died on Friday. He was 75.

Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb hit the blue carpet in a plush charcoal jacket, wide-leg plaid trousers and chunky black boots. A scarf tied to his burgundy leather bag added a pop of color to the pregame look.

Bryce Young goes with a modernized throwback flavor to the late 1990s and early 2000s aesthetic. Think Allen Iverson redefining NBA wardrobe attire with the baggy Reebok track pants and hats with titled swag. The modern unique addition here is the pants appear satin-like look that almost looks like Liquid Metal.

Young doesn't make many statements with his words, but he does it with his actions. And this fit feels like he's tapping back into California childhood energy he grew up on. The LA hat slightly titled to the side shows that element too. It translated to his play as the Panthers put up 30-plus points on Baltimore Ravens.

-- Cameron Wolfe

Thursday night fashion
Texture did the talking in C.J. Stroud's arrival. The Texans quarterback sported a gray knit polo paired with relaxed light-wash jeans, while a black woven bag, brown shoes and a blue-faced watch added the finishing touches.

stories.headline: Vitaly Janelt hits stunner as Brentford stroll to victory over 10-man Everton
stories.summary: Vitaly Janelt scored a 30-yard screamer as Brentford romped to a 4-0 victory against 10-man Everton at the Gtech Community Stadium.
stories.body:
Vitaly Janelt scored a 30-yard screamer as Brentford romped to a 4-0 victory against 10-man Everton at the Gtech Community Stadium.

One win in five had seen some of the early season optimism around Keith Andrews' team fade but this was an emphatic response to fire them up the Premier League table to sixth, even if culpability for Everton's collapse lay largely with James Tarkowski, red carded in the 40th minute for a horror tackle on Yegor Yarmolyuk.

David Moyes was setting a new record for number of games in charge of Everton, this his 593rd match eclipsing the tally Harry Catterick racked up during the 60s and 70s, but this was a terrible first half and was no way to mark such an achievement.

Everything went wrong for the visitors. Both Brentford goals scored by Keane Lewis-Potter came via deflections and Tarkowski's momentary abdication of responsibility as captain, lunging studs-up into the shin of Yarmolyuk with his team 2-0 down, would have been impossible for Moyes to mitigate. He was let down badly by one of his senior players in a moment of direst need.

Thereafter the game was little contest. It might have trickled towards a routine two-goal win for Brentford had Janelt not pulled out a brilliant strike from range that ripped past Jordan Pickford to rub salt in the wound for Moyes, and for Tarkowski.

Fábio Carvalho bundled one in from on the goalline with his knee in stoppage time, the final indignity for Everton.

Brentford were excellent throughout. Early on, Callum Wilson fed Michael Kayode arriving up on the right, the full-back given a clear shot on Pickford's goal but dragging his effort badly across the face and wide.

Everton were making it too easy. Midway through the half they failed to deal with a ball over the top and Jaidon Anthony sent it low into the middle with a deft stab of the toe. It was a beautifully controlled first-time pass, finding Lewis-Potter arriving in an acre of space and his shot spun in off the lunging Jarrad Branthwaite.

It took less than two minutes for Lewis-Potter to hit a near-identical second, with a ball into the box from Mikkel Damsgaard met with unconvincing Everton defending.

The Brentford midfielder was given two attempts, his first shot rebounding back to him to squeeze the ball in at the second go via a deflection off Thierno Barry.

Everton were sinking and their captain abandoned them to their fate. Tarkowski was first shown only a yellow for a studs-up challenge on Yarmolyuk. A single look at a replay confirmed the foul was far more serious, the defender's boot connecting high on the shin of Yarmolyuk's standing leg and his dismissal was inevitable.

Jack Grealish came on to try to raise Everton, his first appearance after five games absent for disciplinary matters.

It made no difference. When Janelt's 30-yard rocket flew past Pickford midway through the second half it was the cue for some away supporters to begin the long journey home, and few of them witnessed Carvalho's stoppage-time tap-in. It had been a chastening night for all connected with their club.

stories.headline: Kevin De Bruyne: Man City achievements will not be tainted if appeal fails
stories.summary: Kevin De Bruyne insists his achievements will not be tainted if Manchester City are stripped of any titles.
stories.body:
Kevin De Bruyne insists his achievements will not be tainted if Manchester City are stripped of any titles.

De Bruyne won a host of honours, including six Premier League crowns and the Champions League, during a glorious 10-year spell at City that ended when he joined Napoli in 2025.

A shadow has since been cast over City's most successful era after the club were found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations in September.

Among the punishments City could face if they fail in an appeal is the removing of some of their honours.

De Bruyne, 35, said he remains proud of the part he played in those triumphs and retains huge affection for the club's owners.

De Bruyne, who is back at the Etihad Stadium as Napoli face City in the Champions League on Tuesday, said at a news conference: "I'm proud of what I've done as a football player, and honestly, this is my club, I love the owners.

"I've even spoken to [chairman] Khaldoon [Al Mubarak] about how to buy a club.

"I have nothing but affection for this club, and that will never change, [the way] the people treated me and my family for 10 years.

"Of course, in life there are rules, but everybody plays on the limit. I played in between the white lines, and I competed with other players, and I had many experiences with my teams, with the players. That's the thing that I value most.

"I've given my all and that's not going to change in my mind. I don't think a lot of people will change in their mind how they view me as a player, or how we played.

"But everybody has their own opinion, I guess. Other people may be 'disgraced' a bit, but I can't change anything about that."

De Bruyne's return to Manchester comes amid reports he is unsettled at Napoli and could seek a move in January.

He did not address his future or speculation about tensions with coach Massimiliano Allegri and some teammates, but he did express frustration at the media reaction to comments by his wife about life in Naples.

- Maresca calls Man City's league slump 'a shame' before De Bruyne reunion

- Champions League Power Rankings before MD5: Who's No. 1?

- Enzo Maresca: Man City denied 'clear' goal in draw with Fulham

He said: "To be honest, I am pretty annoyed. A lot of noise came and a lot of bad reactions to my wife and family. I saw pictures of my house -- I don't think it is OK.

"But it is what it is. Some press created this in Italy, I don't know why. Nobody knows my life, you will never know. It has not been nice for my wife, for my family."

Asked about De Bruyne's future, Allegri said: "As far as Kevin is concerned, we have not spoken about that because at the moment we are caught up in all of these games.

"Over Christmas there will be a short break then the transfer window will open and the club will be open to try and bring in reinforcements. Then it is down to the players and who wants to leave."

stories.headline: MLB free agency tracker: 2026-27 offseason trades, moves
stories.summary: We've got you covered on all the major MLB hot stove signings and trades.
stories.body:
The 2026-27 MLB hot stove was lit just days after the Milwaukee Brewers hoisted the franchise's first World Series championship trophy.

All eyes this winter are on the free agency of two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. But he's not the only one who will make a splash in the market, with Freddy Peralta, Randy Arozarena, Seiya Suzuki and Michael King among the other free agents to watch.

Which teams will go big to contend for the 2027 World Series title? And who will make the trades and signings that have everyone buzzing?

Below is a running list of notable transactions and updates from throughout the MLB offseason.

Grades for every notable offseason move

More: Best fits for top free agents | Latest on Skubal | FA rankings

Nov. 23

The New York Mets continued their spending spree Monday by coming to terms on a one-year deal with first baseman Paul Goldschmidt, a source told ESPN.

stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton: I could have beaten Kimi Antonelli if I was Ferrari No. 1
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton has said he believes he could have won a record eighth world championship this season if Ferrari had prioritised him over teammate Charles Leclerc.
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton has said he believes he could have won a record eighth world championship this season if Ferrari had prioritised him over teammate Charles Leclerc.

Hamilton's claim arrived after he tangled with Leclerc for the second time in three races at the Las Vegas Grand Prix -- a flashpoint Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur described as "completely unacceptable." Leclerc was sanctioned by the stewards for his role in the collision.

Hamilton's maiden win for Ferrari at the seventh round of 23 in Barcelona took him 41 points behind Antonelli, and 40 ahead of Leclerc.

And although Hamilton rejected the notion that he ever called on Ferrari to make him its number one driver, the 41-year-old suggested that, with the right backing from his team, he could have afforded Antonelli a proper run for his money.

"I've never asked to be the number one," Hamilton said. "I genuinely haven't. But there was a point in the season where I was 40 points ahead [of Leclerc] and at that point, the fight was with me and Kimi.

"I was the closest one to him. I was second for a long time in the year, and at that point I needed the backing to make sure we beat Kimi.

"There were a few instances in the season -- where, with the support -- I think we could have beaten Kimi in that battle.

"It's not what I've asked for. But we shouldn't have been able to come together [in Las Vegas]. It should just never happen. I've said everything I can on it. And the question now should be for Ferrari."

Hamilton's chances of finishing runner-up in the standings -- his highest championship position since missing out on his eighth title to Max Verstappen in 2021 -- now look shot following the Dutch driver's brilliant recent form.

- Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc 'unmanageable' - Ferrari boss

- Max Verstappen, George Russell's latest war of words unlikely to stay in Vegas

- Max Verstappen mocks George Russell in brutal outburst: 'So far below my level'

Hamilton is 37 points behind Verstappen with only 50 points left across the remaining rounds, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Hamilton is three points clear of both George Russell and Lando Norris, with Leclerc 17 points adrift.

Russell finished only ninth in Sin City after he pranged the barriers with just two laps remaining when a late move on teammate Antonelli for second backfired.

"I wanted that win," Russell said. "It was a bizarre race, and I went for a high-risk move and paid the price.

"Of course I'm disappointed with the outcome, however, I have no regrets. I fought and knew if I wanted the win, I needed to be in the top two positions into the final laps."

stories.headline: Revisiting sports and pop culture from GTA V's launch
stories.summary: "Grand Theft Auto VI" was released Thursday following a 13-year wait since GTA V.
stories.body:
Peyton Manning was beginning a record-setting season. Joel Embiid had yet to play a college basketball game. And "Breaking Bad" hadn't reached its finale.

That was 4,812 days ago, when "Grand Theft Auto V" arrived on Sept. 17, 2013.

More than 13 years later, "Grand Theft Auto VI" launches Thursday, with athletes and teams counting down to its release -- and looking back at how much has changed.

Houston Rockets center Steven Adams even quipped during media day that performances could be impacted by the game's release.

"So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet. Just for the month of November, performances are going to go down," Adams said.

Before finding out whether Adams' prediction holds up, here's a look at the sports and pop culture landscape when GTA V arrived -- Sept. 17, 2013.

Seattle and Denver were starting their Super Bowl runs

The NFL had just finished its second week and two squads were in the early stages of dominant campaigns: Seattle and Denver.

The Seahawks' defense proved to be its superpower, earning the "Legion of Boom" nickname. Seattle allowed 273.6 yards and 14.4 points per game, both the fewest in the regular season. The Broncos averaged a league-high 457.3 yards and 37.9 points per game, while Peyton Manning tossed an NFL record 5,477 yards plus 55 touchdowns.

Both teams would finish with 13-3 records, setting up a Super Bowl meeting in February 2014. Seattle would emerge victorious on the biggest stage after stifling Denver's offense in a 43-8 victory -- and the seeds of Super Bowl XLVIII were sprouting as GTA V was released.

Miami Heat looking to three-peat

The LeBron James, Dwyane Wade and Chris Bosh Big Three were entering their fourth season as teammates following back-to-back titles.

Miami edged out the San Antonio Spurs in the 2013 NBA Finals, an instant classic. The Heat faced a series clinching defeat in Game 6 before Ray Allen's late 3-pointer sent it into overtime. The extra period ended in a Miami victory to force a Game 7, where it closed out another championship.

The Heat faced the Spurs in a rematch in 2014, and San Antonio got its revenge this time around. But, for two straight summers, Miami reigned supreme.

Five stars preparing to go one-and-done

The 2013 college basketball freshman class had its fair share of heavy hitters.

In March 2013, then-high schoolers Andrew Wiggins and Jabari Parker graced the cover of Slam Magazine with the headline "Young Money: The game's next superstars have arrived." Wiggins and Parker were No. 1 and 2, respectively, in the SC Next rankings, but they were far from the only top prospects.

Joel Embiid, Julius Randle and Aaron Gordon all featured in the top 10 of the rankings as five-star prospects. Each of them, alongside Wiggins and Parker, went one-and-done and were selected in the top 10 of the 2014 NBA draft. Other notable names in the 2013 high school class included twins Aaron and Andrew Harrison, Noah Vonleh and Wayne Selden.

'Breaking Bad' nears its end as 'Roar' rules the charts

One of the greatest TV shows of all time, the final season of "Breaking Bad" aired as GTA V came out.

Two days before its release, the iconic "Ozymandias" episode aired. Series creator Vince Gilligan said that the episode is the "best episode we ever have had or ever will have." It remains one of the highest-rated episodes of the series on IMDB with 9.5 stars.

Pop songs led the way on the Billboard Hot 100 the week GTA V came out. Katy Perry's "Roar" hit No. 1 on Sept. 16, 2013, at the time matching Rihanna for the most No. 1's in the chart's 21-year history at 10. It took six weeks for "Roar" to reach No. 1, then-the fastest No. 1 hit since Perry's "California Gurls" in 2010.

Slotted in at No. 2 was "Blurred Lines" by Robin Thicke featuring T.I. and Pharrell. That track spent 10 weeks on the top before being dethroned. Lorde's "Royals" was at No. 3, while Jay-Z and Justin Timberlake's "Holy Grail" sat at No. 4.

The rest of the songs on the charts' top 10 included: "Wake Me Up!" by Avicii, "Summertime Sadness" by Lana Del Rey vs. Cedric Gervais, "Applause" by Lady Gaga, "Hold On, We're Going Home" by Drake featuring Majid Jordan, "Safe And Sound" by Capital Cities and "Berzerk" by Eminem.

WNBA, MLB teams were building championship legacies

The Minnesota Lynx won their second WNBA championship in 2013, and it would mark the beginning of a dynasty. Minnesota won two more in 2015 and 2017, the latter of which made it four titles in seven seasons as the club also won in 2011. Hall of Famer Maya Moore played a key role in each of the four championships. In 2013, she averaged 20.9 points on 53% shooting in the playoffs.

MLB saw similar dominance in alternating years from the San Francisco Giants. San Francisco missed the postseason in 2013 after World Series titles in 2010 and 2012. Someone privy to a trend could've predicted that the Giants would win it again in 2014 -- which they did. San Francisco hasn't won a World Series since, however.

BCS era coming to a close

College athletics looked entirely different 13 years ago, to say the least.

One of the biggest changes in college football lies in the implementation of the playoff system. Previously, the sport used the BCS rankings for 16 years to determine which two teams would play in the national championship game. That system had its fair share of controversies and came to a close following the 2013 campaign.

Florida State and Auburn made sure the BCS era went out with a bang at the Rose Bowl. Facing a four-point deficit with 1:05 left, Heisman-winning quarterback Jameis Winston led the Seminoles down the field for a game-winning touchdown. Two plays later Florida State closed it out to win 34-31 and clinch its first national championship since 1999 in memorable fashion.

stories.headline: Origin star Young locked in for switch to PNG Chiefs
stories.summary: The PNG Chiefs have confirmed the signing of Hudson Young, with the NSW Origin star to leave Canberra at the end of the 2027 season.
stories.body:
NSW Origin back-rower Hudson Young has ended months of speculation, signing with the PNG Chiefs for their inaugural season.

The 28-year-old Canberra star has inked a deal to become the Chiefs' ninth official signing, the NRL's 19th team confirmed on Monday.

Young will honour the final year of his contract with the Raiders, where he has scored 59 tries across 155 NRL matches, before linking up with the Chiefs in 2028.

The second-rower's acquisition will bolster the Chiefs' forward pack.

"Hudson is a player that every club would like to have," Chiefs general manager of football Michael Chammas said on Monday.

"He is tough, competitive, incredibly consistent and brings an edge that lifts those around him."

Young played every minute of the NSW Blues' 2-1 Origin series win over Queensland this year, scoring two tries and making 115 tackles.

He has tallied six Test caps for Australia, but missed the Kangaroos' victorious 2026 World Cup campaign after rupturing his Achilles tendon in July.

Chiefs coach Willie Peters spent time with Young while working with the Australian Test side in 2025.

"Hudson plays with an aggressive style which I have no doubt the people of Papua New Guinea will love to see," Peters said.

"He will be an important leader in our group, and I look forward to working with him in season 2028 and beyond."

PNG have already signed Joey Manu, Brian To'o, Jarome Luai, Alex Johnston, Zac Lomax, Zac Laybutt, Matty Lees and Connor Watson.

AJ Brimson is poised to be the next cab off the rank, with Gold Coast agreeing to terms with PNG to make him the Chiefs' inaugural fullback.

The former Origin flyer was reportedly spotted playing golf with PNG Prime Minister James Marape while in the country to decide whether to consent to the move.

Former Dolphins No.7 Sean O'Sullivan is also set to join the club after next year's English Super League season.

The Chiefs have also met with Sydney Roosters halfback Sam Walker, and held preliminary talks with Brisbane pair Xavier Willison and Deine Mariner over a potential move.
